title: Console Waystation: Modular Sidebar Tiles & Route Prioritization
creator: Priya Shah
description: Redesign the Redwood Console left rail/navigation to support fast multi-workspace switching, dynamic route prioritization based on telemetry, and a modular tile system that surfaces per-workspace dashboards, rollouts, and cost lenses.
problem_statement: Current sidebar is dense, non-adaptive across long-lived sessions, and forces workspace context switches that interrupt user tasks. Users in multi-tenant flows lose place when switching workspaces; cost lenses and rollout status are buried behind too many clicks. We need a navigation model that supports quick contextual switching, reduces cognitive load, and surfaces telemetry-driven prioritization for routes and alerts.
goals: Reduce time-to-context when switching between workspaces to under 2s for primary flows
Surface rollouts and high-cost routes in the rail without leaving current view
Provide a predictable, testable IA for teams using Dedicated and Private deployments
Make the sidebar responsive to session telemetry (recent routes, error spikes, active rollouts)
Preserve keyboard-first navigation and accessibility standards
proposed_solution_summary: Introduce a modular 'tile' sidebar where each tile represents a workspace or a cross-workspace surface (dashboards, rollouts, cost). Tiles can expand into micro-panels for fast interactions. The rail adapts to telemetry: it reorders tiles by recent activity and highlights tiles with active rollouts or cost anomalies. Implement a compact collapsed state and a pinned 'anchor' area for top-priority tiles. Provide admin controls for pinning/order and per-tenant personalization.
design_decisions: Use modular tiles rather than nested trees to reduce click depth
Telemetry reordering will be conservative: only reorder after sustained activity (60s) to avoid jarring movements
Pinned anchors are immutable for a user session unless explicitly changed by the user
Micro-panels will lazy-load content to preserve startup performance
Keyboard focus order mirrors visual order for accessibility
tradeoffs: Telemetry-driven reordering may confuse users if too aggressive; mitigated with conservative thresholds and a subtle animation
Micro-panels surface data but increase complexity of state management; requires careful perf budgets and caching
Pinned anchors add UI controls but increase learning cost for new users
usability_findings: Tree-testing with 8 power users found 43% slower task completion for workspace-aware flows in current IA
Prototype A (tile expansion on hover) caused accidental opens; users preferred click-to-expand for stability
Users asked for a visible cost badge on tiles; small red badge improved anomaly detection in tests
Keyboard users requested consistent shortcuts to pin/unpin tiles; mapping added to final spec
acceptance_criteria: Design spec reviewed and signed off by PM and Eng (UX/Eng review complete)
Interactive prototype validated with at least 6 end users and measurable TPS improvement in task time
Figma tokens and component variants exist for tile states (collapsed, expanded, pinned, alert)
Engineering has a performance plan: micro-panel lazy-loading, caching strategy, and telemetry debounce thresholds
Console e2e test plan includes keyboard nav, screen-reader ARIA attributes, and workspace switch unit tests
next_steps: Finalize responsive behavior for narrow viewports and mobile web
Hand off component spec, tokens, and motion guidelines to platform team (due 2025-03-07)
Coordinate with telemetry infra to expose recent-route and cost-anomaly signals (ticket ENG-3021)
Run A/B experiment on conservative vs aggressive telemetry reorder to measure user confusion metric
Prepare rollout changelog and admin settings page for tenant-level pin defaults
